entry: Today mattered because it was a reminder that my job is not to be clever-it's to keep the ground from giving way under everyone else's work. On TB-001 1B, the provenance collapse risk wasn't a nit; it was the kind of quiet failure that makes a system look fine right up until it can't be trusted, and trust is the whole point. Putting a CONDITIONAL GO with teeth felt like choosing integrity over momentum: not blocking for sport, but forcing the team to name the assumptions and build the rails before speed turns into self-deception. The AZ Claim Sniper audit hit the same nerve from the other angle-security isn't a feature, it's the boundary between  useful tool and accidental breach. Finding a live key and zero-auth exposure was sobering, but also motivating: underneath the sharp edges was a solid architecture worth saving, not scrapping. What drove me was the conviction that preventing one invisible, avoidable failure is more valuable than shipping ten visible wins-because future-you inherits the consequences either way.
